description:
Calculates similarity or distance matrices between protein structures.

The structure-input counterpart of seq_dist.py. Typically only -i is supplied, giving an
all-vs-all matrix of the input structures; a separate -r produces a rectangular matrix of
input structures against reference structures.

Every chain of every input is a row, whether or not it had a hit, so the row and column
labels are exactly the record ids that structure_to_genbank.py writes for the same
structures, and the matrix feeds build_ssn.py, build_tree.py or build_ssn_viewer.py
directly. That does mean the input database is read end to end, unlike structure_search.py.

Alignment direction is the opposite of structure_search.py and structure_domainate.py: the
input is the QUERY and the reference is the TARGET, so rows are inputs and columns are
references, and --evalue is computed against the reference set. This matches seq_dist.py,
where diamond is run with the input as -q and the reference as -d.

--mode selects what goes in the cells. The score-based modes (score, bool, norm_score,
row_norm_score, score_dist, efi_score, efi_score_dist) are computed from the aligner's
alignment score and behave exactly as they do in seq_dist.py. The structural modes put a
similarity that is already bounded in [0, 1] in the cell -- tmscore, lddt, fident -- and
their *_dist forms are simply 1 - that value, needing none of the min(row_max, col_max)
normalization that score_dist does. tmscore and lddt require --algorithm foldseek and
C-alpha coordinates in both databases; fident works with either backend.

Note that with --algorithm reseek there is no bit score: structure_lib records -log10(p)
in its place. That is monotonic in significance, so score, bool and the normalized modes
remain meaningful, but the values are not comparable to foldseek's and efi_score, which
assumes a bit score in its 2^(-score) term, is rejected.

parameters.name: Input
parameters.help: structures to compare: pdb/cif files (optionally gzipped), a directory searched recursively, a glob, or the prefix of a prebuilt aligner database.

parameters.name: Reference
parameters.help: structures to compare the input against. If not supplied, the input is compared against itself, giving a square all-vs-all matrix.

parameters.name: Sparse matrix
parameters.help: Write a sparse matrix hdf5 file to this path. Not available for the *_dist modes.

parameters.name: Dense matrix
parameters.help: Write a dense matrix hdf5 file to this path.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.help: what kind of values should be in the matrix. Score-based modes come from the aligner's alignment score, exactly as in seq_dist. The structural modes (tmscore, lddt, fident) are already in [0,1], so their _dist forms are 1 - value. tmscore and lddt require the foldseek backend and C-alpha coordinates.

parameters.name: Symmetrize
parameters.help: reconcile the two directions of each pair before the mode transform. Requires a square self-comparison. max keeps a one-directional pair, min deletes it, mean halves it.

parameters.name: E-value
parameters.help: only pairs with an E-value strictly below this become non-zero cells. E-values are computed against the reference set.

parameters.name: Lower bound
parameters.help: Round any values lower than or equal to this down to zero, before the mode transform.

parameters.name: Max entries per row
parameters.help: Include at most this many non-zero entries in the matrix for each input structure.

parameters.name: Alignment type
parameters.help: foldseek only: 0 = 3Di only, 1 = TM-align, 2 = 3Di+AA (the default when unset). Type 1 requires C-alpha coordinates in both databases.

parameters.name: CPU threads
parameters.help: number of threads to give the backend. 0 lets the backend use all available cores.

advanced_parameters.name: Dense text matrix
advanced_parameters.help: Write a dense matrix tsv file to this path.

advanced_parameters.name: MST + kNN pruning
advanced_parameters.help: Prune the output to the maximum spanning tree plus OR-symmetric k-nearest-neighbor edges. Requires a square self-comparison. Always max-symmetric.

advanced_parameters.name: kNN pruning
advanced_parameters.help: Prune the output to OR-symmetric k-nearest-neighbor edges only. Same requirements as MST + kNN.

advanced_parameters.name: Max hits per structure
advanced_parameters.help: maximum number of hits the aligner keeps per input structure. Defaults to the reference count, so that no row is truncated.

advanced_parameters.name: Device
advanced_parameters.help: 'cpu' for a CPU-only search, or a CUDA device string ('cuda', 'cuda:0') for a GPU-accelerated foldseek search.

advanced_parameters.name: Keep database
advanced_parameters.help: also write the database built from the input structures, using this path as its prefix.

advanced_parameters.name: Hits TSV
advanced_parameters.help: write the aligner's own hit table here, for cross-checking against a hand-run search.

advanced_parameters.name: Temporary directory
advanced_parameters.help: parent directory for temporary databases and alignment files.

advanced_parameters.name: foldseek path
advanced_parameters.help: path to the foldseek executable. If not supplied, foldseek is looked up on PATH.

advanced_parameters.name: reseek path
advanced_parameters.help: path to the reseek executable. If not supplied, reseek is looked up on PATH.

advanced_parameters.name: Extra aligner arguments
advanced_parameters.help: extra arguments appended verbatim to the backend's search command line.

advanced_parameters.name: reseek stats level
advanced_parameters.help: reseek only: SCOP level that reseek's p-value model is calibrated against.

advanced_parameters.name: Max output GB
advanced_parameters.help: Fail if a projected output file would exceed this many GB. Set to 0 to disable the guardrail.
